Home / Services / Pet Odor & Stain Removal

Pet Odor & Stain Removal

When the smell keeps coming back.

You've cleaned the spot. You've used the enzyme spray. But every time it's warm or damp, the smell returns. We treat the source as far as the material allows—not only the surface you can see.

Get a Free Quote Call +1 (414) 775-3705
Pet urine & stains Enzyme + extraction Honest expectations

The problem

Surface sprays don't always reach the pad.

Pet accidents often soak past the carpet face into the backing or padding. That is why odor returns when humidity rises even after the visible spot looks clean.

Store products treat what you can see. Professional pet odor work aims at what you can smell—deeper in the fiber structure—while being honest when contamination has gone further than one cleaning can fully reverse.

What we treat

Common pet accident types

Urine in carpet

The most common request. Severity depends on how much liquid reached the pad and how long it sat.

Other organic stains

Vomit, feces, and food-related accidents need different chemistry than simple dirt. We adjust treatment to the stain type when possible.

Area rugs

Rugs can hold odor in the pile and foundation. See also our area rug cleaning page when the whole rug needs cleaning, not only a spot.

Repeated accidents

Multiple old incidents in the same room are harder than a single fresh spot. Results vary; we set expectations before work starts.

How we work

Treat the source, then extract

We inspect, apply appropriate solutions for organic odor and staining, and extract. For severe cases we explain what one visit can realistically achieve and when more work—or replacement—may be the better path.

Source-focused treatment

We go beyond the visible outline of the stain when odor indicates deeper contamination.

Enzyme options

When appropriate for organic odors, we use treatments suited to that type of soiling—not only surface soap.

Extraction

Pull out solution and dissolved soil instead of leaving sticky layers that attract more dirt.

Honest scope

If the pad or subfloor is heavily saturated, carpet cleaning alone may not erase the odor. We say so rather than over-promise.

General carpet cleaning refreshes overall soil and appearance. Pet odor work is more targeted. After floods or leaks (not pet accidents), see water damage restoration.

On site

What the visit includes

01

Locate affected areas

Visual and odor assessment of the reported spots and nearby fibers.

02

Treat

Chemistry matched to stain and odor type as far as conditions allow.

03

Extract

Remove solution and dissolved soil from the treated areas.

04

Review

Results and any recommended next steps explained clearly.

Good to know

Pet odor and stain questions

Can every pet odor be removed in one visit?

Many situations improve a lot in one visit. Severe or old contamination in the pad may need more work—or may not fully clear with cleaning alone.

When does replacement make more sense?

When urine has heavily saturated padding or subfloor, or when the same areas have been soaked repeatedly for a long time, replacement can be more effective than repeated cleanings. We will be direct if that is the case.

Is it safe for pets?

We use products suitable for homes with pets. Keep pets off the area until it is dry.

Do you guarantee 100% odor removal?

No. We work to maximize results and stay honest about limits. Guaranteeing zero odor in every case would not be truthful.

Is this the same as regular carpet cleaning?

No. Carpet cleaning addresses overall soil. Pet odor service targets organic staining and smell. Many homes need both in different areas—see carpet cleaning for whole-room cleaning.

Steam Cleaning

Steam that sanitizes — not just surface moisture.

High-temperature steam cleaning that kills germs and deeply sanitizes surfaces naturally. Ideal for carpets and hard floors when you want more than a light clean.

Hot water extractionDeep sanitizeCarpets & floors

The problem before T.E.G

Light cleaning leaves the deep dirt.

Vacuuming and basic mopping remove surface soil. Allergens, bacteria, and embedded grit stay in the pile and in porous surfaces until heat and extraction reach them.

Professional steam / hot water extraction is designed for that deeper layer.

Our method

Heat, chemistry, and extraction

We use professional equipment that applies heated solution and extracts soil in the same pass. That combination is more effective than consumer steam mops that leave moisture without removing the dirt.

Hot water extraction

Industry-standard deep clean for carpet and many hard surfaces.

Sanitizing effect

Heat helps reduce bacteria and odors when used correctly.

Controlled moisture

Steam cleaning questions

Is steam cleaning the same as carpet cleaning?

Many people use the terms interchangeably. Our steam / hot water extraction is the professional method for deep carpet cleaning and is also used on suitable hard floors when appropriate.

Water Damage Restoration

Water damage cleanup that stops secondary damage.

A leak or spill doesn't only wet the surface — moisture sits in pad, subfloor, and walls. Fast extraction and controlled drying limit mold risk and save what can be saved.

Get a Free Estimate Call Now
Fast extraction24/7 responseCarpet & floor recovery

The problem before T.E.G

Waiting makes the loss bigger.

Standing water wicks into padding and baseboards. Within hours, odors and swelling start. Within days, mold can take hold. DIY fans alone often dry the top and leave the underside wet.

Professional extraction and monitoring are what reduce insurance loss and rebuild cost.

Our method

Extract, dry, then decide what stays

We remove bulk water first, then use controlled drying and moisture checks. Salvageable carpet and floors are cleaned; what can't be saved is documented clearly so you're not guessing.

Rapid water removal

Pumps and extractors pull standing water before it spreads.

Moisture tracking

We measure, not guess, so drying targets stay accurate.

Sanitize & deodorize

Contaminated water needs more than plain extraction.

Clear next steps

Repair vs replace guidance after the emergency phase.

Our process

Step by step, on site

01

Assess & stop source

We identify the wet zones and confirm the leak is under control.

02

Extract standing water

Bulk water removed from carpet, pad, and hard surfaces.

03

Dry & monitor

Air movers and dehumidification as needed until readings stabilize.

04

Clean or document

Salvageable materials cleaned; non-salvageable areas noted for repair.

Good to know

Water damage questions

What should I do first after water reaches carpet or flooring?

Stop the source if it is safe to do so, move valuables out of the wet zone, and avoid walking through contaminated water. Call for extraction as soon as the area is safe to enter—waiting increases secondary damage.

When should professional help be called?

As soon as standing water or soaked carpet is present and the leak is under control. The earlier bulk water is removed, the higher the chance materials can be saved.

What happens to wet carpet?

We extract standing water, then dry and monitor. Salvageable carpet can often be cleaned; padding and heavily saturated areas may not be savable. We document what can stay and what cannot.

When is replacement necessary?

When materials stay wet too long, swell, delaminate, or hold contamination that cleaning cannot reverse. We are direct when replacement is the better path.

What information should I document?

Photos of the source and wet areas, approximate timing of the event, and any steps already taken help with your own records. For installed carpet recovery after the emergency phase, see also carpet cleaning and carpet stretching if buckling develops after drying.

Carpet Stretching & Repair

Loose carpet is a trip hazard — we restretch it properly.

Buckling, wrinkles, and gaps at the wall are more than cosmetic. Power stretching puts the carpet back under the right tension so it lies flat and stays safe.

Get a Free Estimate Call Now
Power stretchWrinkle & buckle repairSafer floors

The problem before T.E.G

Humidity, age, and bad installs loosen carpet.

Carpet expands and contracts. Over time — or after water events — it can ripple, bubble, or pull away from the tack strip. Walking on loose carpet is unsafe and accelerates wear.

Our method

Power stretch, not knee kicks alone

We use proper stretching tools to put tension across the room and reseat edges where needed. Spot knee-kicking is not enough for large loose areas.

Full-room tension

Stretch from the right direction so waves flatten out.

Edge reseat

Carpet is hooked back onto tack strip where it has pulled free.

Seam check

We note open seams that may need separate repair.

Safer walk surface

Goal is a flat, secure floor again.

Our process

Step by step

01

Inspect

Map loose zones, seams, and tack strip condition.

02

Release & stretch

Where needed, edges are released and power-stretched.

03

Secure

Carpet is reseated on the strip and checked for flatness.

04

Advise

If padding or seams need more work, we say so clearly.

Good to know

Carpet stretching questions

Can all buckling be fixed by stretching?

Most humidity and install-related wrinkles can. Severe water damage, delaminated backing, or destroyed tack strip may need replacement instead.

Do you move furniture?

We discuss access when you book. Heavy or fragile items may need to be moved by you first.

Is stretching the same as restretch after cleaning?

Sometimes carpet loosens after cleaning if it was already marginal. Stretching is a separate service when the install has gone slack.

Hardwood Floor Cleaning

Hardwood that looks rich again — without damaging the finish.

Dust mopping isn't enough. Fine grit acts like sandpaper under shoes. We clean and condition finished hardwood so it looks rich again without flooding the boards or stripping the finish.

Get a Free Estimate Call Now
Finish-safeGrit & film removalHomes & offices

The problem before T.E.G

Dirty water and harsh products dull wood fast.

Steam mops and excess water can swell boards and cloud the finish. Grocery-store cleaners leave residue that attracts more dirt. Over time floors look gray even when you clean weekly.

Professional hardwood cleaning uses controlled moisture and the right chemistry for sealed wood.

Our method

Clean for wood — not for tile

We remove loose grit first, then clean with products and methods suited to finished hardwood. No standing water. Optional conditioning where appropriate to restore depth of color.

Grit removal first

Abrasive soil is lifted before it scratches under the pad.

Controlled moisture

No flooding — finish and joints stay protected.

Residue-free clean

No sticky film that re-attracts dirt.

Optional condition

Restore richness on worn high-traffic paths when suitable.

Our process

Step by step, on site

01

Dry soil removal

Dust and grit cleared so cleaning solution isn't grinding particles in.

02

Finish-safe clean

Proper cleaner applied and extracted or wiped per floor type.

03

Detail edges

Baseboards and corners where dust builds up.

04

Inspect & advise

Notes on wear, scratches, or refinish timing if needed.

Good to know

What we don't do

We don't sand or refinish floors — that's a separate trade. We deep-clean finished hardwood so it looks its best between refinishes. Unfinished or waxed floors need different care; tell us the finish type when you book.

Good to know

Hardwood cleaning questions

Can engineered hardwood be cleaned?

Many finished engineered floors can be cleaned with controlled moisture. The wear layer and finish condition matter—tell us the floor type when you book.

What about waxed or specialty finishes?

Waxed and some specialty finishes need different care than modern polyurethane finishes. Share the finish type so we do not use the wrong approach.

How often should hardwood floors be professionally cleaned?

It depends on traffic and soil. Homes with heavy foot traffic or pets may benefit from periodic professional cleaning between routine dust mopping.

What should be avoided on hardwood?

Standing water, steam mops that over-wet joints, and residue-heavy cleaners that leave a film. Those are common causes of dull or damaged finishes.

Do you sand or refinish floors?

No. We deep-clean finished hardwood between refinishes. Sanding and refinishing are separate trades.

What about tile in the same home?

Tile and grout are a different service. See tile & grout cleaning when those floors need attention.
